speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked	the Minister for Education (Schools) whether the Ministry will be accepting and adopting all the suggestions made by the State Coroner to mitigate the risks of suicide and adverse psychological effects for young people under Police investigation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This could be his or her teacher, the year head or the school counsellor.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The school will provide the Police relevant information for all cases to better understand the young person's personal circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Police will inform the parent about the arrest as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Thereafter, the school personnel will keep in touch with the parent to work out the follow-on and follow-up steps to look after the young person's well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This includes monitoring his or her well-being and making counselling support available.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: These efforts by our schools, other Government agencies, parents and the community, will support the well-being of young persons under investigation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The State Coroner suggested that the ideal person would be the school counsellor to be at the interview with the Police, mainly because he would be the resource person and can be the real-time facilitator for communication between the different parties involved.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, by adding in the Appropriate Adults, would this add a new layer that complicates things?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Why not just stick to the school counsellor as the resource or key person to be involved in the process?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For the counsellor in question, he is familiar to the young suspect.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: While a school counsellor may be in a better place to support the well-being of the young person, in those circumstances, he or she may not be neutral.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, that is one part of the answer.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Second, for the school counsellor, whether he or she is accompanying the young adult, a certain level of flexibility would be required, given the school's circumstances.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, beyond the school counsellors specifically, we have decided to include the teacher, or the year head, who is familiar to the student to accompany him or her to the Police station.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In this way, this flexibility will actually have a wider space to support the young person.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: So, the school staff who is accompanying the student to the Police station, he or she will be there the whole time during the interview process?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: He may or may not be there, depending on the circumstances of the event.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When the counsellor, teacher or the year head is at the Police station, there will be a proper handover to the Appropriate Adult.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: If there is no Appropriate Adult present, the school counsellor would have to make a judgement call to stay with the young person until such an adult shows up.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, this would be operational management and we trust the judgement of the school personnel to make the best call.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The basic answer is yes, to a basic level to be able to monitor signs of distress, from the teachers and the year head.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For the counsellors, they will have a little bit more in-depth training.
